target.title: fix(pdf): PDF analysis fails for plugin-provided and bundled-catalog models
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the `pdf` tool fails with "Unknown model" and refuses to analyze a document whenever its selected or fallback PDF model comes from a plugin-provided provider or a bundled-catalog model that has not been materialized into the agent's `models.json`. Users who point PDF analysis at a plugin vision/image provider, or at a catalog-native model, get an error instead of a described PDF even though the exact same provider and model already work for the `image` tool and for normal agent turns.

## Why This Change Was Made

The PDF tool resolved its fallback candidates through a narrow `discoverModels` + registry `find()` lookup, which only sees entries written to `models.json`; it never ran provider runtime hooks and never fell back to the bundled static catalog, so plugin-provided and catalog-native models were invisible to it. This change routes PDF model resolution through the shared `resolveModelAsync(..., { allowBundledStaticCatalogFallback: true })` resolver, the same path the `image` tool (`src/media-understanding/image.ts`) and the main agent loop already use, so PDF resolution now behaves consistently with the rest of the product. The now-unused `resolveModelFromRegistry` helper and its unit test were removed as part of the change.

## User Impact

The `pdf` tool can now analyze documents with plugin-provided providers and bundled-catalog models, matching the behavior users already get from the `image` tool, so configured PDF/vision providers that previously produced "Unknown model" now resolve and run. When a model genuinely cannot be resolved, the failure now carries the richer diagnostics from the shared resolver instead of a bare "Unknown model" string. No configuration changes are required, and there is no behavior change for setups whose PDF model was already present in `models.json`.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests pass locally: `pnpm test src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.test.ts` reports 26/26 passing. The suite was updated so that both the native-provider path and the text-extraction fallback path assert each candidate is resolved through `resolveModelAsync` with `allowBundledStaticCatalogFallback: true` and the workspace dir propagated, which is exactly the behavior that makes plugin-provided and catalog-native models resolvable for the PDF tool.

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  26 passed (26)
   Duration  27.47s
```

This is a convergence onto already-shipped behavior rather than a new resolution path: `src/media-understanding/image.ts` runs `ensureOpenClawModelsJson` and then `resolveModelAsync(..., { allowBundledStaticCatalogFallback: true })`, and `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.ts` consumes the same `{ model, error, authStorage }` result shape, so the PDF tool now matches the resolver contract those paths rely on. After the switch, `resolveModelFromRegistry` had no remaining production callers, so it and its test were deleted, which keeps the net production line count lower than before.
